How to replicate CI configuration locally? Build Chain tool does "simple" maven build(s), the builds are just Maven commands, but because the repositories relates and depends on each other and any change in API or class method could affect several of those repositories there is a need to use [build-chain tool](https://github.com/kiegroup/github-action-build-chain) to handle cross repository builds and be sure that we always use latest version of the code for each repository. [build-chain tool](https://github.com/kiegroup/github-action-build-chain) is a build tool which can be used on command line locally or in Github Actions workflow(s), in case you need to change multiple repositories and send multiple dependent pull requests related with a change you can easily reproduce the same build by executing it on Github hosted environment or locally in your development environment. #### What this PR does / why we need it:

`estimateMinSizeJSON` is a function that is used to estimate the minimum valid size for a given schema node when serialized into JSON (this is used in turn to calculate how many values things like maps and arrays can have). The function works by walking through everything below the schema node it was given, though since `SchemaDeclType` (which is what calls `estimateMinSizeJSON`) is already walking the entire schema and calls `estimateMinSizeJSON` for all arrays/maps, this results in a lot of redundant `estimateMinSizeJSON` calls. This PR removes the need entirely for `estimateMinSizeJSON` by adding a `MinSerializedSize` attribute to `DeclTypes` instead.

The below two tables show the performance gained from this change; the tables were generated with the benchmark included in this branch (the `estimateMinSizeJSON` table used the benchmark patched onto master), with the depth parameter passed to `genNestedSchema` adjusted as per the values in the `n` column. All runs were performed on a 16-core Intel Xeon clocked at 2.3Ghz with 66GB of RAM.

**with estimateMinSizeJSON**

| n (schema depth) | ns/op |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | 538 |
| 5 | 10275 |
| 10 | 385079 |
| 15 | 22950231 |

**with MinSerializedSize**

author: tener
body:
Backport https://github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/14325
---
`app_service` supports two modes: one in which the single process runs `app_service`, `auth` and `proxy`, and the second in which the connection to auth server is done via proxy: it must be able to create a reverse tunnel.

Currently, if we cannot create a reverse tunnel, the `singleProcessModeResolver` is used, but we are not checking the configuration before waiting for all components to come online. If the configuration is invalid, they never will.

This change calls `singleProcessModeResolver` to force the (already existing) check before entering the wait.

Parent: #13969.

body: Currently, it is possible for multiple e2e test to fail when making pull requests when the code is not changed at all. we assume this is because the tests timeout with the current 15 minute threshold. We should increase this threshold to mitigate these intermittent failures to remove the need to rerun tests constantly until they all pass. We can also increase the Github action timeout in order to stop tests from simply cancelling when exceeding 20 minutes.

body:
### Jira Ticket:

NOBUG

### Description:

The `runQuery` and `runScan` functions in `dynamoUtil.js` only run until the DynamoDB Query/Scan limit of 1MB is reached. 
This change leverages `LastEvaluatedKey` to loop through queries/scans until finished if they go over the 1MB limit.

Calling `runQuery` or `runScan` with the `paginated= true` argument will only return the first page of data up to the 1MB limit. 

The functionalites of `runQuery` and `runScan` remain unchanged for existing functions.

author: allyhawkins
body:
Closes #34 and #35. 

Here I added two functions, one for performing highly variable gene selection and one for performing dimensionality reduction on the combined SCE objects that are created in #32. The HVG selection was fairly straight forward since we realized we were able to use the `block` argument to specify the original identify of the cells within the merged object for calculating the variance of the merged object. We noticed that the p-values to identify combined variance normally found with `combineVar` were the same when using `block`. I also added an argument for the number of genes to select, picking the default of 5000 since that's what we were using in #30. 

Now that we are identifying HVG's on the combined object, we also need to update the PCA embeddings, especially since those are what will be used as input into Harmony. We also want to have UMAP on those updated PCA embeddings so we have an unintegrated object to use for comparison. We are also going to need to calculate PCA and UMAP after integration, so we made a function that can be used for dimensionality reduction. This function takes the combined SCE and variable genes as input and calculates both PCA and UMAP. 

I also tried to accommodate for post integration based on what I know so far. So I added an `assay` argument to specify which gene expression matrix should be used for calculating PCA, either "logcounts" or a corrected gene expression matrix. I also have a `do_pca` option which is set to TRUE, but if set to false it will skip PCA and go right to UMAP. This can be used in the case of post integration with Harmony since we will already have corrected PCA embeddings. The last thing I did was add the `prefix` argument so that we can add the type of integration used to the name of the PCA or UMAP embeddings that are stored. For example we can do `fastMNN_PCA` and `fastMNN_UMAP` to signify that those are the results post integration with the `fastMNN` method. 

There still may need to be further modifications made to these functions based on what else we learn from integration but I'm envisioning the workflow would look as follows: 
1. combine SCE
2. calculate HVG
3. dimensionality reduction 
4. integration
5. another round of dimensionality reduction on corrected gene expression or with corrected embeddings

```
name                   old time/op    new time/op    delta
Operation/benchmark-4    93.4µs ± 3%    91.0µs ± 4%   -2.57%  (p=0.006 n=9+10)

name                   old alloc/op   new alloc/op   delta
Operation/benchmark-4    1.59kB ± 0%    1.50kB ± 0%   -6.03%  (p=0.000 n=9+8)

name                   old allocs/op  new allocs/op  delta
Operation/benchmark-4      30.0 ± 0%      27.0 ± 0%  -10.00%  (p=0.000 n=10+10)
```
The benchmark was running against a local live service, so the op time may have noise (e.g. network latency). However, the memory usage and allocation are relatively accurate.

- [ ] Use a streaming manner to consume the wire message to avoid additional memory copies.

author: heversonvasconcelos
body:
### Funcionalidade de registro de log de visualização de Documentos

Desenvolvimento de função para registrar requisições de visualização de Documentos por parte dos usuários.
Atualmente o sistema não possui essa funcionalidade.

#### Extrato do documento de requisitos
##### Objetivo
Implementação referente ao registro de log de visualização de documento em alguns pontos do sistema. Registrar log no sistema após o documento ser exibido. Armazenar no sistema (Banco de Dados) informações de data, hora e usuário / Unidade que visualizou.

#### Referências de código

- https://www.vraptor.org/pt/docs/interceptadores/
- https://github.com/caelum/vraptor/blob/c6a64b3a8940cdfda569caf99cd8fd72952140d3/vraptor-core/src/main/java/br/com/caelum/vraptor/interceptor/DeserializingInterceptor.java
- https://github.com/caelum/vraptor/blob/ac8b7a88d03f88682a5ea03cd4701309f769de38/vraptor-mydvds/src/main/java/br/com/caelum/vraptor/mydvds/interceptor/AuthorizationInterceptor.java
- /sigatp/src/main/java/br/gov/jfrj/siga/tp/interceptor/MotivoLogInterceptor.java
- https://www.baeldung.com/java-log-json-output
- https://github.com/apache/logging-log4j-audit-sample
- https://www.baeldung.com/mdc-in-log4j-2-logback

#### Resumo da implementação

1. Adicionada a anotação @TrackRequest e Interceptor UserRequest para logar as requisições do usuário
2. Método aExibir anotado com @TrackRequest
3. Adicionda a classe UserRequestPayload para encapsular as informações a serem auditadas
4. Adicionado custom Log Level BLAME com id 450 para facilitar a visualização e rastreabilidade dos eventos interceptados
5. Configuração no log4j2.xml para registro de logs serem direcionados para o arquivo sigaex-user-request-track.log. Dessa forma, eventos com log level BLAME ficam separados do arquivo padrão de logs, facilitando assim a ingestão dos dados pelo Logstash ou outra ferramenta utilizada
6. Recurso de Mapped Diagnostic Context (MDC) adicionado para facilitar o registro e formatar o arquivo de logs
7. Adição do appender json-file para gerar arquivo .log.json
8. Adição da configuração REGISTRAR_REQUISICOES_USUARIO e JLogic ExPodeRegistrarRequisicaoUsuario para habilitar ou não o registro das requisições nos logs
9. Adição da função js trackRequest e  método GET registrar_requisicao_usuario para capturar os eventos de cliques nos botões HTML, PDF, PDF Sem Marcas e Tela Cheia da tela Ver Documento Completo e botões Imprimir e Download da tela Visualizar
10. Propriedade logdir adicionada para obter o diretório de logs do jboss (${logdir}/sigaex/user-request-track.log)

#### Exemplo formato dos logs

##### user-request-track.log
`
BLAME 2022-08-05 12:39:34,259 UserRequestInterceptor _Ver Documento Completo [{lotacao=ZZLTEST, matricula=99999, nomeAcao=_Ver Documento Completo, nomePessoa=USUARIO TESTE, requestId=ce261d24-14d4-11ed-973f-f8b156fcacc3, requestParams=nomeAcao=_Ver%20Documento%20Completo&sigla=ZZPRC202200214V01&, requestURL=http://localhost:8080/sigaex/app/expediente/doc/exibirProcesso, sessionId=qbAxZoXKblmdPEqn8eCLH7yFlJPRC1KPFYqNNYQA, sigla=ZZPRC202200214V01, userIpAddress=127.0.0.1}]
`

##### user-request-track.log.json
`
{"timeMillis":1659713974259,"thread":"default task-5","level":"BLAME","loggerName":"br.gov.jfrj.siga.ex.interceptor.UserRequestInterceptor","message":"_Ver Documento Completo","endOfBatch":true,"loggerFqcn":"org.apache.logging.log4j.spi.AbstractLogger","contextMap":{"lotacao":"ZZLTEST","matricula":"99999","nomeAcao":"_Ver Documento Completo","nomePessoa":"USUARIO TESTE","requestId":"ce261d24-14d4-11ed-973f-f8b156fcacc3","requestParams":"nomeAcao=_Ver%20Documento%20Completo&sigla=ZZPRC202200214V01&","requestURL":"http://localhost:8080/sigaex/app/expediente/doc/exibirProcesso","sessionId":"qbAxZoXKblmdPEqn8eCLH7yFlJPRC1KPFYqNNYQA","sigla":"ZZPRC202200214V01","userIpAddress":"127.0.0.1"},"threadId":232,"threadPriority":5}
`

#### Captura de Telas

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1022974/183107038-cd83cc6c-71a5-4302-affe-3bfbc98eb576.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1022974/183106733-db27718d-4e1f-412b-a68a-b295eb76ccb0.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1022974/183106912-505d0600-f3b4-487c-8acc-f66466c5a769.png)


#### Pendências

- [x] Especificar um arquivo para logs e formatar o seu conteúdo
> Configurações efetuadas via arquivo log4j2.xml para formatar e direcionar o fluxo de eventos com log level BLAME direcionados para o arquivo user-request-track.log
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1022974/180768507-2a00d793-91a3-4bdd-b895-0f14aa97ad94.png)

- [x] Avaliar o uso do formato do log em JSON para facilitar a ingestão dos dados pelo Filebeat
> Adição do appender json-file para gerar arquivo .log.json
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1022974/180768726-30f60420-d83f-4ac1-a263-dd27664e7e3d.png)

- [x] Parametrizar a funcionalidade com uma configuração do módulo Siga-Doc
> Adição da configuração REGISTRAR_REQUISICOES_USUARIO
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1022974/182441092-75cf4074-90da-448e-a45b-c4f0aec45c8c.png)

- [x] Obter o id ou nome do botão relacionado a ação do usuário
> Adicionado parâmetro nomeAcaoVO para possibilitar o registro do nome da AcaoVO

### What changes were proposed in this pull request?
<!--
Please clarify what changes you are proposing. The purpose of this section is to outline the changes and how this PR fixes the issue. 
If possible, please consider writing useful notes for better and faster reviews in your PR. See the examples below.
  1. If you refactor some codes with changing classes, showing the class hierarchy will help reviewers.
  2. If you fix some SQL features, you can provide some references of other DBMSes.
  3. If there is design documentation, please add the link.
  4. If there is a discussion in the mailing list, please add the link.
-->
This PR refactors the v2 agg pushdown code. The main change is, now we don't build the `Scan` immediately when pushing agg. We did it so before because we want to know the data schema with agg pushed, then we can add cast when rewriting the query plan after pushdown. But the problem is, we build `Scan` too early and can't push down any more operators, while it's common to see LIMIT/OFFSET after agg.

The idea of the refactor is, we don't need to know the data schema with agg pushed. We just give an expectation (the data type should be the same of Spark agg functions), use it to define the output of `ScanBuilderHolder`, and then rewrite the query plan. Later on, when we build the `Scan` and replace `ScanBuilderHolder` with `DataSourceV2ScanRelation`, we check the actual data schema and add a `Project` to do type cast if necessary.

author: dadlerj
body: I'm not 100% sure who to tag on this—please just let me know if any of you are not the right person! This update does three things: * It (finally) eliminates the old `usagestatsdeprecated` package. For historical context, this was a redis-based precursor to our postgres-based internal event logging architecture. It was removed from most places a long time ago, but has remained the data source behind user counts for billing purposes (i.e., those that admins saw if they went to the Admin > Usage Statistics page, or if they queried users from the API). Why was this left in place for so long? There were concerns in the past that some customers wouldn't be using the postgres-based system, but I don't believe that's even possible anymore. * It updates all calls to that package to use `usagestats` instead. Similar functions already existed, so this didn't require much updating. * However, the `usagestats` package captures more events than the old `usagestatsdeprecated` one did! For example, `usagestats` records events from all users, not just registered ones. `usagestats` records backend events (e.g. the `"ping"` event which is logged every time the instance sends a ping, or events that fire when saved searches run, or events that fire when batch changes are created via API, etc. So I added a parameter to the database functions that return unique user counts to exclude system users. One open question from my end: should I make it so that system users are excluded by default, instead of requiring the dev to set a flag? I also identified a new bug while testing this: https://github.com/sourcegraph/sourcegraph/issues/38825 ## Test plan * Tested in local instance * Validated that all unit tests still worked ...Any other suggestions? ## Screenshots The new admin usage stats page on a fresh instance: The corresponding list of events up to that point: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5589410/178843107-8796ed70-8da8-4f74-8070-1dd9a3a48206.png) Note that even though there are a number of system user events, they are not showing up on the active users page.

author: e-mbrown
body:
Refs #68358

Previously, when the primary region failed the leaseholders would go to
a random region. Secondary regions would provide a failover region that
leaseholders will fail into if the primary region is down. When a
secondary region is set, a secondary lease preference is added to tables
and partitions. This should ensure two voters are moved into the secondary
region

Release justification:
Release note (sql change): CockroachDB now supports secondary regions.
Secondary regions makes it possible to specify a failover region, which
will receive the leaseholder if the primary region fails.

While upgrading to active interaction `5.0.0` I found that the `inputs must be a hash or ActionController::Parameters` argument error is being raised when inputs are composed within an interaction (i.e. `compose(Multiply, inputs)` ). It looks like that error will be raised unless they are a hash or an `ActionController::Parameters` instance when we probably want to also allow them to be `Inputs` for composition. 

I wrote two test cases, one for the `#normalized` method where the error gets raised to make sure it does not when they are of type `ActiveInteraction::Inputs` and one for the `#compose` method directly to ensure it is a valid outcome for both a hash or an `Inputs` instance.

It's my first time reading through the library source, so if I'm missing anything obvious or there is a better way to approach this let me know how I can help!

author: 99warriors
body:
Summary:
change `TracInCP._self_influence_batch_tracincp` and `TracInCP._self_influence_batch_tracincp` `TracInCP._self_influence_batches_tracincp_fast` to be named `self_influence`, which is now public, and now accept a DataLoader yielding batches (as well as a single batch, as before).  The modified helper function can be called by external functions to compute self influence.

The helper itself is also changed to improve efficiency, by reducing the number of times checkpoints are loaded.  The modified helper, despite being able to compute self influence scores for a dataloader yielding batches, still only loads each checkpoint once, per call.  This is because the modified helper now has an outer iteration over checkpoints, and an inner iteration over batches (the order of iteration is reversed compared to before). This helper is called by `influence` when running it in self influence mode.

The reason we cannot just increase the batch size to reduce the number of checkpoint loadings is that for large models (precisely those for which loading checkpoints is expensive), the model takes up too much memory, so that the batch size cannot be too large.

Minor change: for `influence_src_dataset` argument of all `__init__`'s, add description of what assumptions we make of the batches yielded by the dataloader.

Reviewed By: NarineK

Differential Revision: D35603078

If it is a significant code change, please **make sure there is an open issue** for this. 
We work best with you when we have accepted the idea first before you code. -->

<!--- For ALL Contributors 👇 -->

Full disclosure: I don't think we should merge this PR. This PR is meant to demonstrate a rough working solution for code coverage in Workflows and serve as a starting point for discussion, so we can get a coverage solution into samples-typescript and the docs. I just figured this would be a good repo to use since this is what was reported in https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-typescript/issues/729

## What was changed
<!-- Describe what has changed in this PR -->

1. Changed to using Mocha to make it easier to use nyc. That's because nyc stores code coverage state in a user-land global `__coverage__`, which makes it easier to get code coverage state out of the vm sandbox. Jest uses native v8 code coverage by default, which doesn't use `__coverage__` as far as I can tell.
2. Added a `test.coverage` script which, among other things, runs `nyc instrument` on our compiled TypeScript logic in `lib`. This change is important because that makes the Workflow bundler bundle JavaScript that's already instrumented for code coverage.
3. Added a query interceptor which adds an `__coverage__` query that returns the current state of `global.__coverage__`, and an `afterEach()` hook that pulls the coverage info from each test and writes the coverage info from each test to a `coverage/coverage-${workflowId}.json` file.
4. Made `npm run test.coverage` wrap up the coverage output files into one coverage output.

Here's what the output looks like in the shell:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1620265/179075413-712c7b4f-5c2c-4fa1-bca2-60ffdb09911a.png)

and in HTML output:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1620265/179075575-50b1a63b-80db-4f57-938c-96f1708c8fdd.png)

Here's related docs from the Cypress team that I found very helpful: https://docs.cypress.io/guides/tooling/code-coverage#E2E-and-unit-code-coverage

author: junbl
body:
The existing `Key::from` method, which creates a key from a `&[u8]`, panics when the key isn't long enough. This PR moves this logic into an impl of `TryFrom` that returns a `Result` instead of panicking. The existing `Key::from` now just unwraps the `TryFrom` impl, so its behavior is unchanged.

This allows better handling an improperly created key, as well as creating a `Key` without having `Key` in scope, e.g. when using another crate that requires a `Key` but doesn't reexport `cookie`.

author: ehofesmann
body:
There are a few instances in which the CVAT integration scaled poorly in regard to the number of tasks that exist on the CVAT server and the number of annotation runs on a dataset. This PR implements optimizations to improve these issues
Specifically:

1) When loading annotations, the existing tasks were explicitly listed only to determine if a given task id exists. This can take a few minutes if there are thousands of tasks on the CVAT server, which is much longer than any other operation for a small annotation run on only a few samples.
2) When performing operations on the `CVATAnnotationResults` like `get_status()`, it was previously connecting to the API and closing the connection every single time. Now, you can pass in an API object which will be used directly, allowing you to avoid needing to authenticate CVAT credentials every single time you want to `get_status()`, which can be a lot of there are hundreds of annotation runs on a dataset.

author: rjzamora
body:
Following the discussion in https://github.com/dask/dask/pull/8560, I decided to take a pass at revising the `fuse_roots` optimization for `Blockwise` Layers. Whereas the original optimization was relying on low-level fusion, the new version is using `Blockwise.io_deps` to effectively "fuse" simple input tasks that have no other dependencies.

Note that I also fixed some of the existing tests that were inadvertently testing `optimize_blockwise` rather than `fuse_roots`.

author: benilovj
body:
## What's the issue?

This commit fixes a double-counting bug in the "TRN requests by day" and the "TRN requests by month" sections on the performance page.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23801/179075297-14fa2ec1-1c28-4266-8e18-8ef7c56f5c01.png)

In the example above, for July 2022, the sum of the "TRN found", "No match" and "Did not finish" columns is 3,122 requests, but the total column shows 2,931 requests.

## Root cause

For a TRN request that was initially unsuccessful, a Zendesk ticket ID will be populated. Later, when the helpdesk finds the TRN for this user, the TRN will also be populated on the record via the background Zendesk scanning job.

These requests were being double-counted in both the "TRN found" and "No match" categories.

author: jdockerty
body:
Simplify the traversal of commits and make it more efficient.

Previously, I iterated every single commit, even if most of them were skipped using the `CommitIter.ForEach` func. Now, we only loop if the condition is satisfied with our `since` value, this can technically still be every single commit with a large value, but is much better for general use on larger repositories.

It's rather anecdotal, but I tried it myself before this change on a repository like `kubernetes` and the app would simply hang in the terminal. Now it is much faster, since the iteration stops short, rather than iterating every single commit by default.

Also added various commit tests, which are useful for any type of refactoring later.

body:
### Benchmark where identified

- CIS v1.4.0

### Description

This updates the KMS CMK rotation enabled query to skip any KMS keys that are in the `Pending Deletion` state. These keys are marked for deletion, and thus it doesn't matter if rotation is enabled or not, so best to skip them to keep the report clean.

If the key is ever restored and put out of pending deletion, then the state will change and should show up in the report the next time it runs.

author: aetherunbound
body:
## Fixes
<!-- If PR doesn't fully resolve the issue, replace 'Fixes' below with 'Related to'. -->
<!-- If there is no issue being resolved, please consider opening one before creating this pull request. -->
Fixes WordPress/openverse#1531 by @AetherUnbound

## Description
<!-- Concisely describe what the pull request does. -->
<!-- Add screenshots, videos, or other media to show the problem and the solution when appropriate. -->
This PR adds a DAG which captures Elasticsearch metrics for the 72 hours prior to the schedule interval and reports them to slack.

I also took this opportunity to use the [TaskFlow API](https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow/stable/tutorial_taskflow_api.html) for Airflow - it made the actual DAG definition so much simpler! Super useful when all of your steps would otherwise be `PythonOperators`. 

### Additional notes
- This adds a few new variables/connections. With the way this is set up though, nothing (should) need to be modified in production besides adding the `ES_INSTANCE_IDS` Variable.
- This adds a new python package ([PIL](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/)) in order to perform some image manipulation. This means we'll need to publish and deploy a new Docker image in order to actually run this DAG. We could do this as a specific commit, or we could cut and release v1.3.1.
- This adds a new bucket to S3, `openverse-airflow`. This bucket can be used for Airflow entities that don't explicitly relate to the catalog (since `openverse-catalog` almost exclusively has TSVs in it). I've added this bucket by hand for testing, but I recognize that it should probably have a follow-up in the infrastructure repo. @sarayourfriend do you have any insight on where it'd be best to put that?
- I tried to make the DAG agnostic to the number of metrics we're gathering, in case we want to add more in the immediate future.

### Screenshots
**DAG**

deno run --allow-read ./src/get-trigger.ts --source=your-trigger-file.json.

deno run --allow-read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/slackapi/deno-slack-hooks/d9f93add46ccc39bda5aa8ad10a24c88524fcd6e/src/create-trigger.ts --source=your-trigger-file.ts

Simple PR which I originally thought to fix some rare crashing with ISM Custom Data but I believe it was fixed with 5.0.3.

Really just a simple query suggestion/optimization to prevent sending updates to ISMs that aren't being rendered.

This is the mac entitlement config file to be embedded in dart-sdk-darwin-arm64.zip and dart-sdk-darwin-x64.zip. 

dart-sdk is built by copying prebuilt_dart_sdk, which points to files under `prebuilts/`. But prebuilts is a generated folder and it looks like it doesn't have a BUILD.gn file. In this case I am not sure what the leaf node targets would be. So I added them as `contents`(as opposed to `data_keys`) at the parent level (as opposed to at the leaf level). This might not be the correct approach, would be great if the experts could help take a look. Thank you!

author: taxe10
body:
Problem description: When executing a job with very long logs (like the ones in MLCoach), the patch request didn't go through because of the size of the message. In the frontend of the app, this sometimes reflected as "failed" or a lost connection with the container/job.
How it was fixed: The logs are updated according to the portions that have changed only - and with a limit of 50,000 characters - if longer than that, 2 or more patch requests are sent.
This issue needs some more exploring, but this quick fix should work for incoming testing purposes.

author: johnwparent
body:
At the moment, Spack relies on string parsing to determine compression/archive file extension type when fetching/staging packages. Prior to #27021, if Spack was unable to successfully extract a Spack recognized archive/compression extension, it simply tried to use the `tar` system utility. This was generally successful, however with Windows support, a stricter requirement was needed, specifying that Spack be able to successfully parse the extension or raise and exception.  As has been pointed out by #31499 and a number of other issues, this can at times be fragile and occasionally breaks Spack installs. 

This PR resolves this issue in two ways:

- Improvements to the string parsing (minor)
- Magic number parsing

The magic number parsing is the focal point of this PR. Spack will, if file is on filesystem, read magic bytes from binary stream of file, determining filetype/extension from this information. For compressed file types i.e. `.gz` Spack will decompress and peek at the first bytes in order to determine if the underlying file is an archive type i.e. `.tar`. If Spack is unable to decompress the file in memory (if python version does not include LZMA support for example, or the compression is `LZW` or `LZH`), it falls back on simple filepath parsing to check if the file being compressed is an extractable archive.

This behavior is similar to the `file` command, or `libmagic` but is written in cross platform Python, and thus can be used on Windows. Other pure Python implementations of similar functionalities exist, but either have significant drawbacks that would limit their usage in Spack, are overkill, or produce results that are not consistent with what we need Spack to produce. 

Additional changes made in this PR:

- Python native compression utility importing has been refactored to minimize runtime impact of Python import system.
- Tarball handling and documentation updated to reflect transition away from native python module (see #31563)
- Compression test refactored to reflect impact of above changes
- Refactor `file` usage to a more accessible location within Spack
- `decompressor_for` no longer requires both an extension and a file argument as the extension was being derived from the path in all usages.

author: kkysen
body:
When pretty-printing a `Graph`, instead of the `GraphId` index, print the `Graph`'s hash.

The reason we print the hash instead of the index is so that `Graph`s remain stable when their position changes,
 so when changes cause a new `Graph` to be emitted,
 it doesn't cause a snapshot diff on all subsequent `Graph`s, only the new one.

As for the actual hash printed, the hash (a `u64`) is turned into a `u32` and then printed as base64 to be succinct and readable.

# Description

This PR includes the following proposed change(s):

- Determines whether a user is a moderator of the current community
- If the user is a moderator then a 'Flagged Posts' button appears on the right side of the page
- Clicking the 'Flagged Posts' button toggles between seeing all community posts and only flagged posts
- If a post is flagged, a flag icon will be present in the post header next to the title with the tooltip 'Flagged Post'
